a: Cache-aside: app reads cache, on miss loads DB then fills cache.
Read-through: cache layer loads from DB on miss transparently.
Write-through writes to cache and DB together for consistency.
Write-behind writes cache first and asynchronously persists to DB.
TTL expires entries after a duration to bound staleness.
Invalidation removes or updates cache when source data changes.
Keys should include version, tenant, and relevant query dimensions.
Many clients missing the same key stampede the DB; serialize or soft-TTL.
CDN caches responses near users using Cache-Control and surrogate keys.
Cache 'not found' briefly to protect origin from repeated misses.
